turns.doctor_question: Hello, and welcome. I'm Dr. [Name], a psychiatrist. What brings you in to see me today?
turns.patient_response:
Hi. Well, I'm here because I'm having a really hard time at work lately. I do bookkeeping, and I just... I can't stop going back over the same spreadsheets and calculations again and again. 

I end up staying at the office for hours after everyone else leaves. Even when I know I've already checked the numbers, I feel like I have to do it one more time. If I don't, I get this awful feeling that something bad is going to happen, and it'll be my fault. It's just gotten really out of control, and I didn't know what else to do.

symptom_reasoning.S066: The patient describes excessive, repetitive checking of spreadsheets and calculations driven by the need to prevent an awful outcome and self-blame, characteristic of compulsions.

turns.doctor_question: When you feel the urge to check those spreadsheets again, do unwanted thoughts or images pop into your head that make you feel like you have to check — or is it more of a general worry or anxiety that drives you to do it?
turns.patient_response: It's definitely specific thoughts. Like, even after I check and I know the numbers match up, this thought just keeps jumping into my head that I missed one hidden mistake in the payroll or the taxes. I'll start thinking that somebody's check won't go through, or the firm will get in trouble because of me. I try to push the thought away, but it just comes right back. It's like... I can't even trust my own eyes anymore.

symptom_reasoning.S065: The patient describes intrusive, persistent thoughts about hidden mistakes causing harm that repeatedly return despite attempts to suppress them.
